Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

Ça m'amuse = that amuses me. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to amuse'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'amusé').

examples.text: Je suis content que ça t'amuse.
Très bien. Très drôle. Je suis content que ça t'amuse.

examples.text: Je ne veux pas t'empêcher de t'amuser.
examples.trans: I do not want to stop you from having fun.

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to wait (for); to expect'.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!
examples.trans: Wait two minutes for me in front of the office!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
